cf.title: BUG #19723: CREATE INDEX racing with ALTER INDEX ATTACH PARTITION triggers unexpected internal error

input.subject: BUG #19723: CREATE INDEX racing with ALTER INDEX ATTACH PARTITION triggers unexpected internal error

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducer and a bisect in message #1, and the fix is local to DefineIndex(). The one design concern, new blocking or deadlock in v1, was raised in message #4 and answered there with a fast-path check plus a recheck after locking. Which version to commit and the back-patch range are still open.

brief.title: Recheck partition index attachment after locking it in CREATE INDEX
brief.problem: CREATE INDEX on a partitioned table can fail with "bogus pg_inherit row" when it races with ALTER INDEX ... ATTACH PARTITION on a partition's index. The reporter reproduced it on 19beta4 and bisected it to commit 8b08f7d48. Users who run both commands at the same time get an internal error (XX000).
brief.proposed_design: DefineIndex() calls has_superclass() on a partition's existing index before it locks that index, so a concurrent ATTACH can commit while CREATE INDEX waits for the lock. v1 takes the lock first, then checks. Rafia Sabih's version keeps the unlocked check as a fast path and checks again after taking the lock, and adds an isolation test.
author_claims: has_superclass() requires the caller to hold a lock on the child index, and DefineIndex() calls it without one.
Locking the child index before the check fixes the reported race in the author's testing.
Rafia Sabih says v1 makes CREATE INDEX on the parent wait on, or deadlock with, sessions holding locks on an already attached index, where unpatched it completes.
Rafia Sabih says the fast-path check plus a recheck after locking avoids that new blocking.
brief.thread_state: Rafia Sabih reviewed v1, found a deadlock it introduces, and posted an alternative patch with an isolation test. The author has not replied to it, and no committer has commented.
unclear: The material does not show the commit message or touched files of Rafia Sabih's patch.
Nobody says which branches carry commit 8b08f7d48, so the back-patch range is not stated.
The thread does not say whether other has_superclass() or partition attach paths have the same unlocked check.
Nobody says whether the recheck version can still block when the index is attached during the lock wait.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The fix stops DefineIndex() from attempting a conflicting pg_inherits row; it adds no catalog change.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry targets stable branches, but nobody says which branches carry commit 8b08f7d48.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch changes lock order in DefineIndex() in src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c, which future changes to that loop must preserve.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which branches carry commit 8b08f7d48, and so which branches need this fix?
Does the author agree to replace v1 with the fast-path check plus recheck from message #4, given the deadlock that message reports for v1?
Can the recheck version still block or deadlock when ALTER INDEX ... ATTACH PARTITION commits during the lock wait on the child index?
Do other callers of has_superclass(), or other partition attach paths, make the same check without holding a lock on the child?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows partitioned index DDL and the lock rules in DefineIndex() would have to own it; none has commented in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the lock order in DefineIndex() on every branch that gets the fix, including any new blocking or deadlock that shows up in the field after a minor release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a diff and then a patch file within two days, but has not replied to the review and alternative patch in message #4.

priority.reason: The bug needs CREATE INDEX on a partitioned table to race with ALTER INDEX ... ATTACH PARTITION, so few users hit it, but it is a reproducible internal error bisected to a recent commit. The fix touches one file and adds no user-visible surface.

provisional_note: The commit message, touched files and code of the recheck patch in message #4 were not shown, so its locking behaviour and its isolation test could not be checked. The back-patch range also depends on where 8b08f7d48 landed.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for partitioned tables. It first creates catalog entries for all partition indexes as invalid, then builds and validates them the way REINDEX CONCURRENTLY does, so an interrupted run leaves INVALID indexes that DROP or REINDEX can clean up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages are reviews and fixes from mid-2024 with no stated objection, and in October 2024 a user asked why progress had stalled; the entry was withdrawn in April 2025 with no visible closing message.

precedents_retrieved.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets create index concurrently work on partitioned tables by first creating catalog entries for all partition indexes with indisvalid=false, then building each one concurrently. An interrupted run leaves invalid indexes that the user can clean up with DROP or REINDEX, as with CIC on a plain table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last shown message, from Alexander Pyhalov in July 2023, asks whether releasing the session lock on the parent table between child index builds is safe, and no reply is shown. No committer review appears in the thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY support for partitioned indexes. It changes index_drop() to expand a partitioned index into the list of its partition indexes and run the concurrent drop steps on all of them in two transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier disliked the new code path for deleting dependent objects in the partition tree and said the problem needed more design work first. The patch then stopped applying to HEAD, and the author withdrew it until the related patch for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned tables makes progress.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking
quicky at the patch, I am not much a fan of the new code path
introduced for the deletion of dependent objects in the partition
tree, so my gut is telling me that we need to think harder about the
problem at hand first.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for ATTACH PARTITION
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes psql tab completion after "ALTER TABLE <table_name> ATTACH PARTITION" so that it lists foreign tables as well as ordinary tables. Before the patch, foreign tables were missing from the list.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera asked for a more precise completion query that leaves out relations that cannot be attached: existing partitions, and parents or children in legacy inheritance. David Zhang also asked to filter out tables that are already attached. The author posted no updated patch, so vignesh C marked the entry Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For example, any
relation that's already a partition cannot be attached; as can't any
relation that is involved in legacy inheritance as either parent or
child.

precedents_retrieved.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change how MergeAttributes() handles column compression and storage settings under table inheritance, treating them as physical per-table properties. A new child inherits the parent's settings but can override them, attaching a child changes nothing, and conflicting settings from multiple parents require an explicit setting in the child.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We have already discovered with the previous attempt that
there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage.  Also, there
isn't even a patch yet.

precedents_retrieved.title: Autovacuum (analyze) on partitioned tables for ATTACH/DETACH/DROP commands
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch proposed counting the live tuples of a partition toward its partitioned ancestors' changes_since_analyze when the partition is attached, detached or dropped, so that autovacuum would trigger an analyze on the partitioned table after these DDL operations. It added three configuration parameters (autovacuum_analyze_attach_partition, autovacuum_analyze_detach_partition, autovacuum_analyze_drop_partition) to enable or disable the behavior, with reporting done via pgstat_report_anl_ancestors().
precedents_retrieved.objection: No design objections appear in the visible messages. The patch stopped applying to HEAD, a rebase was requested, and the author did not respond for four weeks, so the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Four weeks later, nothing has happened.  So I have marked the patch as
RwF.

precedents_retrieved.title: Automatic HASH and LIST partition creation
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION BY with a clause (stubbed as CONFIGURATION) that automatically creates a set of HASH partitions from a modulus or LIST partitions from a list of value sets. Partitions are generated as additional CREATE TABLE statements during parse transformation, named tablename_N, with RANGE support and deferred (on-insert) creation left for later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected that supporting LIST and HASH but not RANGE was not a good idea and that a design covering all three strategies was needed. He also questioned the CONFIGURATION syntax and the automatic partition naming convention. The thread then stalled with review comments unanswered, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think it's a very good idea to support LIST and HASH but not
RANGE. We need a design that can work for all three partitioning
strategies, even if we don't have support for all of them in the
initial patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
Reverted commit(s): Reject concurrent sequence refreshes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f38afa4abb04e85530c94b88daf11c089375daca.

That commit fixed a race that could leave stale sequence values on the
subscriber after 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. It did so by
raising an ERROR during 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'
whenever a sequence synchronization worker was already running for the
subscription.

That approach caused intermittent buildfarm failures, because the existing
tests did not ensure the sequencesync worker had stopped before executing
'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. While discussing how to fix
the tests, we concluded that blocking the command while a sequencesync
worker is running is inconvenient for users. So we will fix the original
race differently in a follow-up commit.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: [P15] is a sequence-sync race fix reverted for blocking a command, a different area and mechanism. The thread cites no earlier attempt, and the new blocking that v1 adds was raised and answered in message #4 by the fast-path check plus recheck.

No standards or compatibility objection. The fix adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump output or psql change. The one user-visible regression, v1 making CREATE INDEX on the parent block or deadlock on already attached indexes, was raised in message #4. The recheck version there takes no lock beyond what unpatched code takes, so the concern looks settled. [P15] is a different area and does not apply. Without the code, one point cannot be checked: whether 8b08f7d48 is only in 19, which sets the back-patch range.

Both versions change only lock order and add a recheck in DefineIndex(), with no new on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column, protocol message or exported struct, so nothing blocks a back-patch on ABI grounds. The fix stops a race from attempting a conflicting pg_inherits row, which protects catalog consistency.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It moves a lock acquisition and adds a recheck inside DefineIndex() for an index the caller already has the right to build on. It adds no new privilege, view, error text or default, and it lets no user see or do anything new. The one new blocking case, from v1, was raised in message #4 and is handled by the fast-path recheck. Any session that can hold conflicting locks on a child index can already block CREATE INDEX on the parent through the partition table lock, so no new denial-of-service path follows. [P15] is about a different subsystem and does not apply.

This is a small, local bug fix in DefineIndex(). It adds no new GUC, catalog state, API or dependency, and costs nothing on any common path. The one design concern, new blocking in v1, was raised in message #4 and answered there by the fast-path check plus recheck. [P15] matches only on topic: it was reverted because the fix blocked users, and the recheck version avoids exactly that. A committer may still ask whether other has_superclass() callers make the same unlocked check, but the material gives no failure scenario for them.

This is a fix for an internal error ("bogus pg_inherit row") in DefineIndex() when it races with ALTER INDEX ... ATTACH PARTITION. No existing feature, option, extension or external tool can stand in for a race fix inside core DDL code, and neither version adds a second mechanism. Precedent [P15] is about blocking sequence refreshes, so its reason does not apply here.

This is a bug fix for an internal error (XX000, "bogus pg_inherit row") that a reporter reproduced with a script in message #1 and bisected to a recent commit, so the problem is real and stated. A demand objection does not apply to a fix for a race in ordinary DDL; the open design question, the new blocking found in message #4, belongs to other angles.
